note: Scored members are evacetrapib, DRL-17822 and rocacetrapib (CKD-519); the record rests on evacetrapib, whose transgenic-mouse lipid prediction held in patients while its outcome trial (ACCELERATE) found no benefit.
label: Hyperlipidemia (CETP)

engagement.note: Evacetrapib inhibited plasma CETP ex vivo in human CETP/apoA-I transgenic mice (ED50 under 5 mg/kg) and raised HDL-C.
engagement.quote: In double transgenic mice expressing human CETP and apoAI, evacetrapib exhibited an ex vivo CETP inhibition ED(50) of less than 5 mg/kg at 8 h post oral dose and significantly elevated HDL cholesterol.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed); full text not retrieved.

engagement.note: Healthy volunteers on evacetrapib had 65-91% trough CETP inhibition and HDL-C up 87% at 600 mg, the mouse readout reproduced in people.
engagement.quote: The trough inhibition of cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) activity was 65 and 84% at 100 and 300 mg, respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; human study run by the sponsor that made the mouse data.
engagement.reason: CETP activity fell in dosed humans
engagement.judgement: Readout matched to the mouse's own PD readout (ex-vivo plasma CETP activity), so readout_tier direct; the HDL-C rise in patients (Nicholls 2011) is the efficacy endpoint here and is not counted twice. Paired by me: the Suico abstract does not mention the mouse. Mouse ED50 is in mg/kg and human data in mg, with no exposure bridge given, so magnitude direction_only. No NCT record found for this multiple-ascending-dose study (searched LY2484595 and evacetrapib, start before 2011).

dose.model: Human CETP/apoA-I transgenic mouse; rat blood pressure
dose.note: Mouse set the effective dose (ex-vivo CETP ED50 under 5 mg/kg); rats at high exposure multiples showed no blood-pressure rise, a stated margin.
dose.short: Mouse ED50; rat BP margin stated
dose.quote: Importantly, no blood pressure elevation was observed in rats dosed with evacetrapib at high exposure multiples compared with the positive control, torcetrapib.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; exposure multiples not given in the abstract.

dose.model: Human CETP/apoA-I transgenic mouse; rat blood pressure
dose.note: Humans reached 91% CETP inhibition at 600 mg with no change in 24-h ambulatory blood pressure, so target and margin both held.
dose.quote: Evacetrapib at the highest dose tested did not produce any significant effect on 24-h ambulatory systolic or diastolic blood pressure.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the rat study stated a tolerated exposure well above the effective one (no BP rise at high exposure multiples), and humans were dosed to deep CETP inhibition without BP change, so same with margin_stated. The lipid surrogate then responded (efficacy same), so dose is not derived_from efficacy despite the null outcome trial. ACCELERATE's 130 mg later showed SBP +1.2 mmHg vs placebo (NEJM 2017 results text), which the authors call small next to torcetrapib's 5.4 mmHg; I did not count it as a margin failure. Rocacetrapib: an animal allometric PK/PD model (hamster, rat, monkey; Choi 2019, https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics11070336, abstract) predicted a 25 mg efficacious dose but missed human bioavailability badly; it is a different model of a different member and does not change the best-model status, so it is not an entry.
dose.magnitude_basis: CETP inhibition at dose; BP at tolerated exposure

efficacy.note: Mice carrying human CETP and apoA-I were the in-vivo model for evacetrapib's HDL-raising effect.
efficacy.quote: In double transgenic mice expressing human CETP and apoAI, evacetrapib exhibited an ex vivo CETP inhibition ED(50) of less than 5 mg/kg at 8 h post oral dose and significantly elevated HDL cholesterol.

efficacy.note: In 398 dyslipidaemic patients evacetrapib raised HDL-C 54-129% and cut LDL-C 14-36%, the co-primary endpoints; ACCELERATE later found no fewer cardiovascular events.
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo or statin monotherapy, evacetrapib as monotherapy or in combination with statins increased HDL-C levels and decreased LDL-C levels.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed); JAMA full text not read.
efficacy.reason: Lipid surrogate matched; outcomes trial null
efficacy.judgement: The model predicted a lipid surrogate (HDL-C), and in a hyperlipidaemia context the phase 2 co-primary endpoints (HDL-C, LDL-C % change) are the disease's own endpoints, so the status follows them; ACCELERATE (Lincoff 2017, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1609581; NCT01687998, results posted 2018-05-16; HR 1.01, stopped for futility) sets outcome_tested negative. ACCELERATE enrolled high-risk vascular disease, not a lipid-selected population. I did not use the cholesterol-fed rabbit atherosclerosis model: it was run with non-member drugs (JTT-705, torcetrapib) and I found no evacetrapib atherosclerosis study or statement that Lilly relied on it. Paired by me; the JAMA abstract does not cite the mouse. Mouse HDL rise is not quantified in the abstract, so direction_only.

patient_trials.quote: Although the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib had favorable effects on established lipid biomarkers, treatment with evacetrapib did not result in a lower rate of cardiovascular events than placebo among patients with high-risk vascular disease.
DRL-17822 phase 2 in type II hyperlipidaemia, primary endpoint percent change in HDL-C at 28 days: placebo 3.2%, 50 mg 84.2%, 150 mg 122.1%, 300 mg 160.6% (registry results table).

safety.model: Rat blood pressure + human adrenal H295R cells
safety.note: Unlike torcetrapib, evacetrapib raised neither rat blood pressure nor aldosterone or cortisol synthesis in adrenal H295R cells: a stated prediction of no off-target harm.
safety.short: Predicted no BP or aldosterone rise
safety.quote: Importantly, no blood pressure elevation was observed in rats dosed with evacetrapib at high exposure multiples compared with the positive control, torcetrapib.

safety.model: Rat blood pressure + human adrenal H295R cells
safety.note: At 600 mg humans showed no 24-h blood-pressure or mineralocorticoid change; ACCELERATE later saw only +1.2 mmHg systolic.
safety.quote: Evacetrapib was devoid of clinically relevant effects on blood pressure and mineralocorticoid levels.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; ACCELERATE BP figure from the NEJM results text seen as a search excerpt.
safety.reason: No torcetrapib-like BP harm in humans
safety.judgement: The model's stated prediction was absence of torcetrapib's off-target BP and aldosterone effect; healthy volunteers bore it out. ACCELERATE (12,092 patients, 130 mg) found SBP 1.2 mmHg higher than placebo, which the authors call small against torcetrapib's 5.4 mmHg and unlikely to affect outcomes; I kept same rather than add a partial entry. DRL-17822 phase 2 (NCT01388816) reports vital-sign changes in 1-2 patients per arm, consistent. Paired by me (Suico does not cite the rat data).
